script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 5. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

When you learned to read, your brain literally rewired itself.  Areas that evolved for recognizing faces and tracking objects were repurposed to decode squiggles into meaning.  Reading is a hack—using ancient brain machinery for a brand new trick.

Learning to read creates new neural pathways. Brain scans show readers develop enhanced connections between visual, language, and meaning areas. Your brain today is physically different because you learned to read. Reading doesn't just change visual processing—it changes how you process spoken language too.  Literate people hear speech differently than non-readers.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Skills reshape the brain.  Reading is proof that what you practice, you become.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Reading as Brain Training - Choose Your Input.

Here's your activity: Choose something to read today—a book, a long article, anything requiring sustained attention. As you read, remember: you're not just absorbing information, you're reshaping your brain. What kind of brain are you building? This helps you view reading as active brain development.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what reading does to your brain can be applied to reading as brain training - choose your input. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
